newsitem.title: USA: CME Aug pork bellies close limit up on Japan talk.
newsitem.headline: CME Aug pork bellies close limit up on Japan talk.

text.p: CME pork bellies closed the three cent limit up in the key August contract, boosted by talk of Japanese buying interest, floor sources said.
"There is some talk of Japanese interest in the bellies but I don't know if it is true," one dealer said.
There was a pool of unfilled buy-orders in the August contract of 160 cars and also a pool in July of 60 cars.
"The usage between now and mid-August (in Japan) is pretty strong so a lot of people think they are buying some extra to fill in for needs," said analyst Chuck Levitt of Alaron Trading Corp.
He noted that Japan's Obon holiday, which extends through mid-August, is normally a period of high meat consumption.
August closed the three cent limit up at 84.10 cents a lb and options prices indicated a synthetic close of 84.70 cents, options traders said.
There was also talk of Japanese demand for loins.
Other traded months ended up 3.00 to 1.975 cents.
Floor sources said E.D. and F. Man International, Lind Waldock and R.J. O'Brien were all featured buyers of the August contract.
Hog futures also closed sharply higher.
Dealers said the run-up in hogs was partly fuelled by short covering amid indications the market was oversold following the recent decline.
"Futures were just undervalued compared to cash," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities.
August futures closed up 1.550 cents a lb at 81.50 cents. Prices had been falling since early last week, dipping from a session high on July 15 of 82.05 cents from a low on Wednesday of 79.75 cents.
Cash hogs remained weak with prices down $1.00 to $1.50 Thursday and expected to be $0.50 to $1.00 lower on Friday.

Floor sources said LIT were a late buyer of August hogs, Cargill Investor Services and Rand Financial Services commercial desk were buyers of October and R.B. and H. Financial Services were a noted buyer of December.
Locals were net sellers of August and Saul Stone was a featured seller of December, they added, noting that selling interest in October was scattered.
